candidate.answerReason: The stated position of E makes the parallel ray toward BD split the required angle into 30° and 40°, giving 70°.

methods.label: Draw a parallel through E
methods.explanation: Through point \(E\), draw \(EF\parallel AB\). Then \(EF\parallel CD\), \(\angle BEF=\angle B=30^\circ\), and \(\angle DEF=\angle D=40^\circ\), so \(\angle BED=30^\circ+40^\circ=70^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: Uses grade-7 auxiliary parallel construction, parallel-line properties and angle addition.

methods.label: Use triangle BDE
methods.explanation:
Triangle \(BDE\) gives the required angle once we find the sum of its other two angles. Let \(\alpha=\angle ABD\) and \(\beta=\angle CDB\). Since \(AB\parallel CD\), these same-side interior angles satisfy \(\alpha+\beta=180^\circ\). The stated position of \(E\) means \(BE\) splits \(\angle ABD\) and \(DE\) splits \(\angle CDB\). Therefore,
\[
\angle EBD+\angle BDE=(\alpha-30^\circ)+(\beta-40^\circ)=110^\circ.
\]
The angles of triangle \(BDE\) sum to \(180^\circ\), so \(\angle BED=180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ\).
methods.levelReason: Uses grade-7 parallel-line properties and the primary-school triangle angle sum; no more advanced theorem is needed.

The attached figure agrees with the stated same-side condition; no right angle at B or D is assumed.
